dedupe_keys.name: household food waste survey of tulcan ecuador 582 households 2023

description: This survey records how much food households in the Ecuadorian border city of Tulcán throw away, why, and what they do with it, linked to how they shop and store food. The producers are Gabriela Revelo, Orlando Meneses, Mikaela Narvaez, Jenny Yambay and Freddy Torres of the Universidad Politécnica Estatal del Carchi. Coverage is 582 households in the urban area of Tulcán interviewed in person in June 2023. The de-identified table has 41 variables on household size and composition, purchasing and storage habits, weekly food spending, whether and how much food was wasted, the causes people give, and disposal routes such as feeding animals, composting or the municipal collection. The compendium also includes the sampling frame, data dictionary, questionnaire and interviewer manual, method protocol and R analysis script, and is available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: amounts are self-reported, not weighed, and a single city in one month limits seasonal and national inference. Simulation uses: setting household food waste rates and behaviours in agent-based or demand models of food supply and organic waste collection. Related records: the FAO Food Loss and Waste Database (data-fao-food-loss-and-waste-database) compiles national estimates.
